original_question: For 0 < beta < 1, define the one-dimensional discrete centered fractional maximal operator by M_beta f(n) = sup_{r>=0} (2r+1)^{beta-1} sum_{k=-r}^r |f(n+k)|, where the supremum is over nonnegative integers r, and let q = 1/(1-beta). If f : Z -> R has bounded variation and M_beta f is not identically infinite, is there a universal constant C such that the q-variation of M_beta f satisfies Var_q(M_beta f) <= C Var(f)?
target_in_paper: Section 6.1, Question 10: the open problem asking for the centered discrete fractional analogue of the uncentered variation inequality in Theorem 6.3.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct setting and almost the exact official question: one-dimensional discrete centered fractional maximal operator on Z, parameter range 0 < beta < 1, the exponent q = 1/(1-beta), input f of bounded variation, the finiteness assumption that M_beta f is not identically infinite, and the desired estimate controlling the q-variation of M_beta f by the total variation of f. This is exactly the centered discrete fractional open problem recorded in the paper.
missing_details: The paper relies on the discrete definition of q-variation, which should be stated explicitly for stand-alone completeness: Var_q(g) = (sum over n in Z of |g(n+1)-g(n)|^q)^(1/q).
The total variation of f on Z should be made explicit: Var(f) = sum over n in Z of |f(n+1)-f(n)|.
The paper has a standing convention that all functions are real-valued; stating f: Z -> R makes the question fully paper-faithful.
It helps to make the universal quantifier explicit: the inequality is asked to hold for every such f.
The paper places this question specifically as the centered counterpart of the uncentered discrete result in Theorem 6.3, so that contextual scope should be retained and not broadened.
refined_question: Let 0 < beta < 1 and set q = 1/(1-beta). For a real-valued function f: Z -> R with bounded variation, meaning Var(f) := sum_{n in Z} |f(n+1)-f(n)| < infinity, define the one-dimensional centered discrete fractional maximal operator by M_beta f(n) := sup_{r in Z_{>=0}} (2r+1)^{beta-1} sum_{k=-r}^r |f(n+k)|, and assume that M_beta f is not identically infinite. If for g: Z -> R we define its discrete q-variation by Var_q(g) := (sum_{n in Z} |g(n+1)-g(n)|^q)^(1/q), must there exist a universal constant C > 0 such that Var_q(M_beta f) <= C Var(f) for every such f?
justification: The nearest official formulation in arXiv:1912.04625 is Section 6.1, Question 10. The paper first introduces q-variation in Section 5 and then, in Section 6.1, defines the discrete centered and uncentered fractional maximal operators, states the uncentered discrete bound in Theorem 6.3, and immediately records the centered version as an open problem. Your draft is therefore already very close to the paper's exact intent; the only real gaps are the explicit definitions of discrete q-variation and discrete total variation, plus the paper's standing real-valued convention. No explicit equivalent reformulation of Question 10 is given in the paper.
